page: Amazon Web Services m9g.12xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System and ARMv9 architecture. The instance is powered by dedicated AWS Neoverse-V3 cores running at 3.3 GHz, providing 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. It includes 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The configuration includes 48 MB of L3 cache, a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, and hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. No local storage or discrete GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute and memory throughput. The instance ranks in the top tier for multi-core Geekbench tasks (28111.0), Clang software compilation (92735.0), and both single-threaded and multi-threaded data compression routines. Memory subsystem benchmarks also show high throughput, with PassMark memory scoring in the top tier alongside 136.27 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, general-purpose LLM token processing and inference rates remain in the median tier, indicating that workloads requiring heavy vector or tensor compute may face limits compared to specialized accelerator platforms.

From an operational efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical core design offers predictable execution across dense threads without multithreading contention. With its balanced ratio of memory to processor allocation and 25 Gbps network interface, the m9g.12xlarge addresses in-memory caching layers, Clang and CI/CD build farms, static web serving, containerized application clusters, and relational or key-value databases.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro System using 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. It delivers 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz alongside 192.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, hardware AES encryption support, and 48 MB of L3 cache, but includes no bundled local NVMe storage or dedicated graphics processing units. In benchmark evaluations, the m9g.12xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core Geekbench performance, strong compilation capability in Clang, and exceptional throughput in Redis and static web serving tests, while large language model processing remains average. Because each vCPU corresponds directly to an independent physical core without hyperthreading, the hardware provides consistent resource allocation. This architecture supports demanding multi-threaded workloads, including database servers, continuous integration build pipelines, in-memory key-value caches, and distributed web microservices.
